The unknown parameters are estimated from real-time experiments by using the least squares identification algorithm. The conventional control strategy for this class of systems is the nonlinearity inversion method, which is including an exact inverse of the static nonlinearity into the appropriate place. Hence, any standard linear controller can be applied. In contrast, the performance of this classical control strategy becomes limited when the considered static nonlinearity is not exactly invertible. To overcome this difficulty, a novel control approach is proposed in this paper. An electrical process is considered to illustrate the efficacy of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Performance ADC Flash Based on Bulk-Driven Quasi-Floating Gate Current Mirror
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A new high-performance analog to digital converter flash (ADC) in terms of supply voltage, power consumption, and frequency is proposed in this paper. This ADC is based on a novel Bulk-Driven Quasi-Floating Gate (BD-QFG) current mirror (CM) structure. The workability of the proposed ADC has been verified through ELDO simulations based on a 0.18 μm process. It achieves an enhanced conversion frequency (2.2 GHz), low power consumption (159 μW) from a low supply voltage (0.8 V).

articleTitle: Multi-atlas based segmentation of human cerebellum
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Atlas-based segmentation is a high-level technique which provides highly accurate results particularly in the anatomical segmentation of medical images. The main idea of this technique consists in using a dataset of atlases which is perceived as a priori information necessary for providing the automatic segmentation of images. In the current state of the art of atlas-based techniques, the segmentation task is carried out based on a fixed database of atlases. In this article, we propose a multi-atlas segmentation method for brain MRI images based on a dynamic atlas database which is progressively updated each time a new case is added. The experiments show that the suggested technique seems to perform well compared to conventional multi-atlas based segmentation methods.

articleTitle: Advanced Controls of HVDC Interconnection for Ancillary Services Support
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper proposes advanced controls to improve ancillary services of High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) interconnections. The converters control is a synchronverter-based control (SHVDC). The main goal is to improve the SHVDC controls to comply with the Grid Code Requirements (GCR) set by the Tunisian grid operator, the Tunisian Company of Electricity and Gas (STEG). Two control strategies are proposed. A local/decentralized control and a global/centralized control. The local control regulates voltage and frequency at the HVDC converters point of connection (PoC) to the grid. Frequency and voltage controls are based on conventional droop controls. The centralized control responds to control signals, emanating from the transmission system operator, to render the SHVDC system participate in the grid support as conventional generators. The proposed controls feature operation with energy reserves, emergency control and P/Q ramp-ups and ramp-downs controls. Centralized and decentralized controls are successfully implemented and tested on the HVDC interconnection between Tunisia and Italy.

articleTitle: Immunosensor based on MWNT and Au Nanoparticles for detection of 17ß- estradiol in pg/mL
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Endocrine Disturbing Chemicals (EDC's) are rising class of environmental pollutants that disturb the human body functions. One of the main EDC's is the estrogen and estrogen-like chemicals especially the 178-estradiol (E2). Elevated levels of E2 may develop severe effects on humans and the wild life even in Pico molar level. Therefore, there is an increased demand to sensitively, precisely and affordably detect E2 in an easy and compatible with Point-Of-Care (POC) devices. In this work, sensitive electrochemical immunosensor was developed in pg/ml range with LOD = 1 pg/mL. The screen-printed working electrode surface of the electrochemical sensor was modified with carboxylated Multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) to amplify the electrical signal by simple drop casting in layer by layer manner. The anti-17β-estradiol antibody, supplied as ascites fluid, dilution was optimized to achieve higher sensitivity using covalent immobilization with the carboxyl group of the MWCNTs. The electrochemical characterization of the sensor has revealed that the sensor is able to linearly detect 17β-E2 in the pg/ml range from 1 - 1000 pg/mL. The prepared sensor is simply fabricated, has low cost, sensitive and compatible with point-of-care devices.

articleTitle: Carbon Screen Printed Electrodes Functionalized with Cu(II)Pc for Phosphate Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper is a feasibility study of carbon screen printed electrodes functionalized with copper (II) phthalocyanines (Cu(II)Pc) for phosphate (HPO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) detection. The dispersion of CuPc was studied first of all in Tetrahydrofuran (THF) and Dimethylformamide (DMF). The functionalization of the electrodes was done by drop-casting of CuPc solution into the working electrode. Then, the electrochemical behaviour was tested with ferri/ferrocyanide redox couple in order to study the enhancement of the electrode response after modification. Also, in the presence and absence of HPO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>- the CuPc modified electrode was investigated by different electrochemical techniques: Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) and Differential Pulse Voltammetry (DPV). Results prove the strong interaction between the metallic center Cu and HPO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-, which is translated by the augmentation of the oxidation peak of Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ in presence of HPO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-. Based on found results, the sensor's performances will be calculated (limit of detection, sensitivity, linear range ...) and further studies like stability and selectivity test will be continued.

articleTitle: Drosophila image Segmentation using Marker Controlled Watershed
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Automatic segmentation of biological image is an important step to understand a biological process. Moreover, the task is difficult due to ambiguous boundaries and intensity inhomogeneity. The Marker Controlled Watershed (MCW), was introduced for biological image segmentation as an alternative to the Watershed algorithm which suffers from oversegmentation. However, in the basic version of the MCW, the chosen markers directly impacts the segmentation performance. In this paper a new algorithm is proposed and applied for Drosophila image segmentation. The idea is to consider the characteristic of Drosophila image and use kernels of cells as objects markers. The Kernels are constructed using the Fiji software. The performance of the proposed algorithm is attested and compared to the basic version of the MCW. Results show the efficiency of the proposed algorithm for Drosophila image segmentation in term of the Dice coefficient and F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> measure.

articleTitle: Mechanical Fault Detection of Industrial Electrical Process by Self Organizing Map
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper a diagnosis approach based on Self Organizing Map is proposed for gear fault diagnosis. For this purpose, to investigate technique requires the vibration measurement which through their analysis the gear fault is detected and diagnosed. The details of the analytical method adopted and its principle are clearly presented and its application is experimentally validated using real vibration measurements. The results have an agreement with the real results.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Variable Speed DMC-DFIM Electric Drive System
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this study, analysis and discussion of a Least Mean Square Errors (LMSE) algorithm used for three-phase direct matrix converter (DMC) feeding a doubly-fed induction motor. For this purpose, the model of doubly fed induction motor and the LMSE modulation technique are presented. Subsequently, the entire chain DMC and DFIM are tested using MatLab/Simulik software environment. The analysis of the performances of the results obtained by simulation are carried out on the basis of the following assessment by harmonics spectrum of motor current and the Total Harmonics Distortion (THD) for unbalanced input voltages.

articleTitle: Non-fragile H∞ Observer for a class of Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we adopt a useful methodology (i.e., Lyapunov stability theory and LMI approach) to design a non-fragile observer for a class of nonlinear systems. The observer gain is found directly from the LMI formulation. A numerical example is given to illustrate the use of our method.

articleTitle: Invariable Filter Response Of Metamaterial Layer For Electromagnetic Interference Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient metamaterial single layer structure is presented to achieve an isotropic band-pass filtering response. This layer can be combined with antenna in order to enhance his performance and it is commonly known as Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) structures. The proposed FSS design is a transmitter filter which provide a 3-db fractional bandwidth of a 1.65 GHz around 3.5 GHz resonant frequency. Moreover, simulation results carried out with CST software, demonstrates that this design has a stable frequency behavior at normal and oblique angles of incidents up to 45° both for Transverse Electric (TE) and Transverse Magnetic (TM) wave modes. So, it can be a good candidate for Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) mitigation for 5G wireless applications.

Author Keywords: polarization and angle of incidence independent

articleTitle: Sensorless Control Strategy for Five-Phase PMSM based on UIO for Linear Parameter Varying System
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Sensorless control strategy of five-phase (PMSM): Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor is suggested in this work. A developed model of the Unknown Input Observer (UIO) for Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) system is proposed. This model is investigated for the state and disturbance estimation in terms to improve the dynamic performance of the drive and for more robustness and efficiency. Existence, stability and convergence conditions of the unknown input observer are given in a set of (LMI),: Linear Matrix Inequality and the demonstration are done through Schur complement, and Lyapunov analysis.

Author Keywords: Linear Matrix Inequality and Schur complement

articleTitle: IoT devices in smart grids
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this article, we focus on smart power grids, which are critical in building smart city architectures, especially devices in Transmission Networks (TNs) and Distribution Networks (DN) which are becoming smarter, and therefore more dynamic. The security control of these networks requires the knowledge in real-time of their key parameters which are voltage and current magnitude, and angle differences in these networks. This identification is the main function of Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) in TNs and Micro Phasor measurement units (PMUs) in DNs. These tools send and receive data automatically and with the advent of Global Positioning System (GPS) and the IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP) for time synchronization of these devices, they can be installed in any node in the grids, therefore, µPMUs and PMUs become inevitable IoT devices in power networks.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a novel ultrasound imaging methods for high frame rate echocardiography
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we evaluate two new methods of ultrasound imaging that could be used in cardiac imaging. These methods are Parallel Divergent Waves in the same direction and Parallel Divergent Waves in different directions. We compare these methods with Consecutive Divergent Waves in different directions using a compounding option. The goal of our work is to increase the frame rate of the ultrasound system. Simulation results prove that image quality for parallel emissions could be at the same level as consecutive emissions but without estimating interference, crosstalk and cross-correlation between signals.

articleTitle: SVM-based Inter Prediction Mode Decision for HEVC
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Over the recent years, machine learning technology has witnessed a big progress in many disciplines, particularly in video processing and computer vision. The latest video coding standard is the High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC). HEVC doubles the video compression ratio at the same video quality and without any degradation, compared to its predecessor, H.264/AVC. However, this high performance is reached by increasing the HEVC encoding complexity, mainly due to its coding structure, named quadtree. That's why HEVC complexity reduction presents a crucial subject. To reduce this complexity, this paper proposes a fast Coding Unit algorithm based on Support Vector Machine (SVM). Simulation results prove that the proposed approach can reduce the computational complexity by 52.4% with 1.62 % BitRate degradation and a negligible loss in terms of PSNR using Low-Delay P configuration. However, the proposed scheme achieves a best tradeoff between both complexity reduction and RD performance, comparing to the earliest HEVC framework.

articleTitle: Effects of Airgap Static Eccentricity in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors by Means of Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) static eccentricity faults on the air gap flux density, flux linkage, electromotive forces (EMFs) and electromagnetic torque (EM torque) have been presented. A 2D finite element method (FEM) is needed for PMSM modeling under healthy and faulty conditions. The achieved simulation results under different static eccentricity severities show how eccentricity affect the performance of the studied motor.

articleTitle: Toward a Binarization Framework resolving the Maghrebian Font Database challenges
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Historical documents are of major importance in conserving cultural and scientific heritage. The Maghrebian font of the Arabic language had dominated in different countries. Thousands of cultural and scientific documents were written using this style. In this paper, we intend to present the built Maghrebian font database with giving the different challenges facing the development of an Optical Character Recognition system able to treat it. Also, we are going to reveal the new developed binarization framework, based on Deep Learning theory, able to get the best accuracy compared to different studied binarization approaches. The proposed framework is based on Selectional Auto-Encoders and the Energy minimization theory. The obtained binarization result on the Maghrebian font using the F -measure is 98,1%.

articleTitle: Distributed Q-learning based-Decentralized Resource Allocation for Future Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The next generation (5G) wireless network is expected to support the fourth industrial revolution, combining heightened data transfer speeds and processing power. Despite technological progress, the most important evolution of future networks is the network-densification technique. This technique reduces significantly the propagation distance and makes signal propagation transit from long- to short-range propagation. In this regard, several imposed challenges such as mobility and interference management, and network and resource management can drain the spatial resources and degrade network performance and end user Quality of Service (QoS), when the network density exceeds a critical density. We focus in this paper on the resources management and allocation in the context of exploiting the spatial reuse. However, Nodes are authorized to modify their transmission power (TP) and channel according to the resulting throughput. Toward this goal, a distributed Q-learning, from the Reinforcement learning category (RL), is proposed to allow nodes to select their TP and the channel only depending on their bit rate rewards. Simulation result proves, after having evaluated the effect of the learning parameters, the effectiveness of the proposed method in finding the best-performing configurations in terms of throughput maximization.

articleTitle: Effect of NB-PLC Channel Models on Transfer Function Estimation in Industrial Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper determines the best channel model that estimates well the power line channel compared to the other models studied in narrowband frequency in the industrial environment. These models are multipath, random generator, voltage ratio and tow-port (ABCD) approaches. Simulations based on IEEE 1901.2 PHY layer parameters and Mean Square Error criterion show that bottom-up approach has higher performance than the multipath and random generator methods with a difference of about 5 dB. As a tradeoff between complexity and performance, the multipath model is chosen.

articleTitle: Evaluation of transmit/receive apodization scheme for hardware implementation used in B-mode ultrasound imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: For B-mode phased array ultrasound imaging, Sidelobes are skirts of ultrasound waves around the main lobe. Sidelobes degrade image quality by decreasing Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), Contrast Ratio (CR) and spatial resolution. By using an apodization function that applies different amplifications to the transmitted and received signals we can increase the width of the main lobe and reduce the level of the sidelobes. In this paper, we evaluate the tradeoffs between performance metrics and computational cost for ten windowing functions. Performance evaluation is based on the image quality metrics for Point Spread Function (PSF) and Cyst Phantom (CP) simulations by measuring the spatial resolution, CR, Contrast to Noise Ratio (CNR) and the Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) metrics for each window function output image. On the other hand, we estimate the computational cost by measuring the FLOPS (Floating Points Operations per Second). B-mode simulations prove that Flattop/Nuttall couple gives the highest CNR value in comparison with the other couples for the optimum computation cost.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Self-Tuning PI Speed Regulator for DTC of Three-Level Inverter fed IM
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper reveals a design method to enhance the speed profile of an induction motor (IM) drive fed by three level voltage source inverter (VSI) under direct torque control (DTC). Given that the conventional proportional integral (PI) controller cannot handle the abrupt load variation, we suggest inserting an accurate fuzzy self-tuning PI speed regulator to overcome this limitation. This latter is better than the fixed gains PI controller in terms of robustness against load disturbance. The holistic approach of DTC control scheme combined with the proposed adjustable speed PI controller gains using a fuzzy logic regulator is elaborated and developed. Simulation results verifying the feasibility and effectiveness of the propounded technique is carried out through MATLAB/Simulink software.

articleTitle: Dynamic Deployment of Virtualized Network Function - From Concept to Realization
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Evolving technologies over the last decade have to a great extend enabled us to meet communication requirements of the envisioned application domains of smart cities. Software Defined Networking (SDN), Network Function Virtualization (NFV), and cloud computing are some of the prominent enabling technologies in this regard. This paper demonstrates the interplay of these enabling technologies and contributes with a service orchestrator. The major focus of paper remains on detailing the technical aspects of the enabling technologies and their potential interplay for different application domains. We also discuss the need for dynamic deployment of vNFs in future mobile networks. In this connection, we compose a use case and implement it on an extensively developed validation framework.

articleTitle: A comparative study between three epileptic high frequency oscillations detection strategies
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In the past few years, visual detection of High Frequency Oscillations (HFOs) has led to a good understanding of the fundamental neural mechanisms underlying epileptic phenomena. However, visual marking of HFOs is very tedious, extremely time consuming and remains a subjective process. In addition, some factors like low signal-to-noise ratio and presence of artifacts in electroencephalographic signals make scoring of HFOs a difficult task. Therefore, automatic HFOs detectors have been developed by different research groups with the goal of providing reliable detection results. However, no common dataset was used to evaluate the performance of these detectors. The aim of the present study is thus to provide a fair comparative study of three existing HFOs detectors. These detectors are respectively based on the root mean square, the short time line length and the Hilbert transform techniques. This fair comparative study is performed using a common dataset with the same expert visual marking. The behavior of the considered HFOs detectors is evaluated in terms of the sensitivity, the precision, the false discovery rate and the area under the ROC curve. Our results show that the Hilbert transform based method is the most efficient and reliable method for detecting HFOs compared to the other ones.

articleTitle: Towards an Integration of “SmartHome” Technology in Education: Realization of a didactic platform
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: With the emergence of smart technologies, home automation becomes one of the most interesting fields. In this context, an educational platform of a smart home featured with a multi-sensors system and actuators is proposed along with all realization steps. The platform is resulted from didactic applications intended for higher education students. Configured functionalities and operation modes are explicitly presented in order to satisfy household requirements which are essentially home automation, energy management, comfort and safe access to the house. In this paper, sensors technology, embedded electronics tools and remotely communication modules are exploited to reach to these requirements.

articleTitle: New Energy Efficient Clustering Method Based on Fuzzy Logic and Genetic Algorithm in IoT Network
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is an emergent smart technology which has a significant interest in the modern wireless communications field. Besides, the vast evolution of these networks, there are different issues. One of them is the source energy limited to the capacity of the sensor node's battery. Clustering in IoT network can improve the energy efficiency since that transmission energy is attached to the distance between transmitter and receiver. In this work, we proposed a new clustering approach for IoT network by using the Fuzzy Logic (FL) in IoT'node and the Genetic Algorithm (GA) in the Base Station. In our proposed method, first step includes the nomination process for being a cluster head (CH) and the second step includes the selection of the optimal among the qualified nodes as a CH for that particular cluster. Thus, the nomination method is based on the FL approach and selection CH method is based GA. Simulation results prove that the proposed method performs better than LEACH, PSO and GA protocols, reduces mainly energy consumption and enhances the network lifetime.

articleTitle: Design, modelling and control of an owl-inspired unmanned vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A novel design of an unmanned vehicle inspired of an owl's flight structure is proposed in this paper. Owls are specific birds characterized by silent flight thanks to a comb that ends some of their feathers. Their downy and dense plumage absorbs noises. An owl-inspired robot in a standing posture was proposed and studied lately [15]. In this work, a particular trirotor vehicle inspired of owls in their specific flight is designed. First, a careful observation of the anatomy of owls in their flight drives us to devise a concept based on a drone with three rotors, two motors fixed on the free ends of wings and the third is placed on the head for small deviations. Next, flight phenomenon is explained using kinematics and aerodynamics laws and theories. Control strategies based on classic and intelligent methods are then developed to ensure trajectory tracking and reach desired positions. The last section wraps up the conclusion and provides new perspectives for future works.

articleTitle: Modeling and frequency control of grid connected including wind farm and pumped storage
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The development of energy storage systems is emerging as a predominant sector for renewable energy applications. In this context, this study deals with a grid connected system including a wind farm and a pumped storage hydro plant (PHES). An energy management system (EMS) is proposed to supervise the storage and to ensure an economic profit. A primary and secondary frequency control is investigated. Precise economic and frequency indicators assess the efficiency of the EMS. Simulations demonstrate that it meets the desired targets in terms of compliance with the production program while respecting the various constraints of electric grid management (power smoothing, frequency regulation, etc.).

articleTitle: Proposal for MAC frame parameter design based on OFDM signaling and synchronization error criteria
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Nowadays, communication systems are usually implemented by digital modulated waveforms. Such is the case of OFDM, where the spectrum efficiency and the robustness against undesirable channel effects are the main reported advantages to improve the quality and data rate of transmission. However, OFDM demands for accurate synchronization methods, otherwise intersymbol and intercarrier interference will degrade the achievable capacity of the transmission. The impact of synchronization errors must be considered while designing a system based on OFDM waveforms for the performance guarantee. In this direction, this work addresses a selection strategy of main MAC frame parameters regarding preamble and payload length under OFDM signal transmission with synchronization errors. This selection strategy is proposed to assist designers in the choice of proper MAC frame parameters that best fits into their own restrictions.

articleTitle: Energy Management and Control of a Photovoltaic System Connected to the Electrical Network
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper provides a more detailed and analysis of the energy management of a photovoltaic system connected to the electrical network where the storage system is planned to meet the energy requirement of a three-phase AC load. The structure and modeling of the proposed conversion structure is an integral part of the content of this paper. Then, to validate the desired behaviour, three possible operating scenarios are considered and their discussion presented. Finally, the system was established and analyzed in MatLab/Simulink environment under several conditions such as temperature and irradiance.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Optimal Control for Quadrotors
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this work, the altitude control of a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle is treated using its altitude dynamics in hover mode. Due to persistent aerodynamic disturbances, the control of a quadrotor unit is cumbersome; especially, the ground wake effect which comes into play during landing. In this work, an Active Disturbance Rejection and Optimal Controller (ADROC) modified from an Active disturbance rejection controller (ADRC) is proposed to compensate for undesirable effects resulting in smoother control. The adaptation of the ADRC controller is governed by a Least-Means-Square (LMS) algorithm on the extended state observer (ESO). The ESO linearizes the system and finally, an LQR policy is utilized to find optimal control signal for landing and take-off of the quadrotor.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Control for Uncertain Nonlinear System Against additive and multiplicative Actuator Faults
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, a fault-tolerant control, based on backstepping theory is applied for an uncertain non-linear system with the presence of combined actuator faults (additive and loss of efficiency). This control will be applied to an Inverted-Pendulum System with parametric uncertainties, in order to see its performances with regard to uncertainties and in the presence of defects.

articleTitle: Simulation models in electronic learning systems developed for the control of interactive audiovisual students
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Our work focuses on one of the main actors in distance education who is the Tutor who intervenes to help the learner in critical situations of decision-making in his learning path. Our goal is to integrate an emotion recognition system into the tutor module of the e-Iearning platform to automate the task of tutoring. MOODLE platform is the online learning environment used. This platform is called “open and remote drive systems”, it has a user-friendly interface easy to manipulate by actors using it. Moodle is organized in blocks and has a modular architecture that makes it easy to add new blocks. Our goal is to contribute to the creation of an automatic tutor who can make the right decisions to guide the learner during a learning situation. These decisions are based on emotions extracted using an audiovisual Emotion Recognition System (ERS). For the design of this ERS system, we used two modeling approaches. The first approach is the workflow to model the decision-making block and the second is the connectionist approach used to model the emotion recognition block using a neural network. The system uses several algorithms for the analysis of the audiovisual information of which we cite PCA and MFCC.

articleTitle: Output - feedback Controller Design for Networked Control Systems Subject to Transmission Delays
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The present paper focus on an output-feedback controller design for a distant process in which the loop is closed via a digital network. This latter involves unknown but limited delays in both measurement and actuation channels that poses more challenges. Considering this network constraint, Networked Control System (NCS) can be reformulated as an input time-varying delay system. By consequence, stabilisation problem of global system is investigated using Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMI) approach. Finally, simulation studies support the theoretical develops.

articleTitle: System level design of third order Continuous-Time Sigma-Delta Modulator
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper,a new system-level design of Third-order Continuous-time Sigma-Delta modulator is proposed. The synthesis parameters and topology choice are important and based on the computation of Signal Transfer Function STF and the Noise Transfer Function NTF. The non-idealities of the building blocks are studied such integrator DC gain, Gain Bandwith, Excess loop Delay and jitter. The M topology is chosen in order to achieve the specifications of LTE Standard, within 10 MHz signal bandwidth and clocked at 491,52MHz.

articleTitle: A comparison between two methods for MISO fractional models estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper proposes two new methods for multiple input-single output system identification with fractional models: the instrumental variable based method and the output-error based method. The fractional orders are supposed known and the linear coefficients are estimated. A comparative study between the developed methods is illustrated via a numerical example. Monte Carlo simulations are used to demonstrate the efficiency of the two methods.

articleTitle: Fault Estimation of Nonlinear Time Varying Delay System
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The paper deals with the design of SMO for a class of nonlinear uncertain time delay system. In which, the nonlinearities satisfies the Lipschitz condition, the time delay is varied and bounded and the uncertainty is increased. After design, this SMO is able to give a robust state estimation. Also, our intent isto combine the SMO concept with Lyaponov-Krasovski approach to reconstruct the actuator fault with LMI optimization. Numerical example is provided to illustrate the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Optimized Synchronization Technique for Single Phase Grid-connected Converters
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The performances of the synchronization unit have become a crucial issue in applications involving grid-connected power converters.In view of the topologies of modern power systems, control algorithm of Distributed Generation (DG) sources are required to respond effectively to grid faults in order to support and enhance the stability of the grid. Thus, improving the accuracy and the robustness of the synchronization method during normal or distorted conditions is important to fulfill these requirements. The objective of this paper is to improve the performances of a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) through an optimized tuning of the PI controller. This synchronization technique is based on a second order generalized integrator and it is intended for single-phase Photovoltaic (PV) systems. Its performances are evaluated by simulating its behavior during grid faults. An experimental prototype is developed to validate the operation of the synchronization unit when connected to the single-phase grid.

articleTitle: SVPWM Algorithm for a Delta Inverters-fed double-star induction machine
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The aim of the present paper is to study the feeding of a Double-Star Induction Machine (DSIM) by two three-switch three-phase inverter. In this trend an improved SVPWM control strategy dedicated to a reduced delta inverter has been applied to each used inverter. A simulation model of the DSIM motor is developed in a Matlab/Simulink environment. The simulation results illustrate the validity of the proposed electrical model and approve the reliability to feed the DSIM motor by the delta structure inverter.

articleTitle: Shunt Active Power Filter based on Artificial Neural Networks for Grid-connected Photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to improve the quality of the energy generated by photovoltaic grid-connected system. In order to compensate harmonic currents caused by nonlinear loads and to reduce total harmonic distortion (THD), shunt active power filter, based on multilayer feed forward neural networks and fuzzy logic techniques, is used. The performance of the proposed control model is verified by MATLAB based simulation results. Results are compared with the instantaneous reactive power technique results.

articleTitle: Three Tank System Identification Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In order to determine an exact model of the three tank system, this paper presents an optimization method based on the genetic algorithm (GA). This method let us find the best parameters of this system while reducing the quadratic error between simulated and measured outputs.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Monitoring Approach Based on P-time Petri Nets of manufacturing Systems with Time Constraints
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Manufacturing job-shops can have uncertainties related to different operations. A time interval is associated with each operation compose of two limits: the minimum time required to perform the operation and a maximum time not to exceed in order to ensure the quality of the manufactured products. The fuzzy sets can be applied to many fields in which uncertainty plays a key role [1]. The uncertain knowledge associated with these discrete event system with time constrains requires specific reasoning and modeling methods. Fuzzy logic provides a framework for the exploitation of fuzzy knowledge, which from a qualitative point of view gives finer results than classical logic. The paper proposes a new approach for monitoring and maintenance of manufacturing systems with time constraints that integrates fuzzy logic and P-time Petri nets (P-TPN) tool. So, in this context, we propose a new fuzzy Petri net able to analyze monitoring and recovery tasks of a discrete event system with time constraints, using a temporal fuzzy approach. The monitoring module is consists of P-time PNs and fault tree. The first is used as modeling tool of normal behavior of the system. The second model corresponds to monitoring model. Finally, to illustrate the effectiveness and accuracy of proposed monitoring approach an application to a winding unit is outlined.

articleTitle: Fusion of classifiers based on physical activities data from smartphone user
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The behavior recognition of mobile phone users is based on different types of smartphone sensors. The accelerometer is one of these sensors which can represent the person activity. In this paper, in order to recognize and classify the physical activities of user's smartphones, we will use the Dempster-Shafer (DS) theory of belief functions. After applying decision tree machine learning algorithm on each of the three axis of movement, we will fuse different combinations of these results. Then, we will fuse different machine learning algorithms applied on three axis of movement together. We will show that using a classifier of each attribute give better results than applying on all attributes.

articleTitle: Boundary conditions at interfaces for the case of thin semi conductive layer on insulating surface
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The main purpose of this work is the discussion of interface condition according to the media beside the interface for the case of insulator covered with thin layer of pollution subjected to electric field stress. The deposit of pollution on the insulator surface is treated as a semiconductive thin layer and boundary conditions are described for cases of interfaces between: dielectric/conductor, dielectric/dielectric, semi conductive/dielectric and demi conductive/conductor. The charge densities at the interfaces change over time. Gaussian equation which involves the difference between electrical induction vectors and Maxwell equation is used. Influence of surface conductivity and permittivity of the thin layer on potential distribution is investigated for the case of 2D linear insulator model subjected to DC high voltage.

articleTitle: Improved Sensor FDI using AC ripple signals analysis of the d-axis component of the line current
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Satisfactory operation performance of electrical systems depends heavily on different factors, namely sensors accuracy and system components. This paper presents easy fault detection, isolation method against currents measurement failure for grid connected photovoltaic system, were DC offset, and scaling errors are considered. This method does not need any extra hardware. It is based on analytical analysis of d-axis components of line current at the grid angular frequency ωg and 2ωg. These components are extracted through band pass filters in order to generate two residuals, which are employed for fault detection and isolation. Simulation results present the effectiveness of the proposed technique. An experimental platform was carried out to validate the obtained simulations results.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of a Pendulum based Converter for Energy Harvesting from Random Vibration
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Challenges associated with implementing energy harvesters as an alternative power supply for wireless networks are mainly related to their performance under ambient sources. In this paper, a vibration energy harvester, which is able to generate relatively high level and regular output under any applied excitations, is presented. The converter operating principle is based on including an intermediate storage stage in form of mechanical energy similarly to conventional harvesters in wrist watches. The converter is composed of a pendulum, a spiral torsion spring, gear set and a DC generator. The dynamic behaviour of the pendulum is studied based on finite element analysis including the effect of friction at the joint. A physical model of the converter components is developed and evaluated comparing the experimental results to demonstrate its validity.

articleTitle: Decentralized Control Synthesis for Interconnected LTV Systems using Shifted Legendre Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, a new technique of decentralized control synthesis for linear time variant systems is proposed by using orthogonal functions. Making use of this mathematical tool allows primarily to transform the interconnected time-varying parameters differential state equations to a set of algebraic coupled ones. This is done by expanding the system input and output variables over a shifted Legendre polynomials basis and then computations are carried with the help of orthogonal basis operational matrices and Kronecker product properties. The decentralized state feedback control parameters for the interconnected linear time variant system is therefore determined by minimizing the gap between the closed loop system and a chosen linear reference model outputs coefficients in the orthogonal basis.

articleTitle: Single,Double and Quadruple Maximum Power Point Trackers for a Stand-Alone Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a simulation based study of single, double and quadruple maximum power point trackers for determining the global maximum power point GMPP under partial shading conditions for a solar photovoltaic system using MATLAB/SIMSCAPE. Traditional single MPP trackers are less efficient than double MPP trackers and have a higher sensitivity to partial shading. By using double MPP trackers, several features can be obtained, such as the possibility of connecting two arrays with different string sizes or different solar azimuths or tilts within high efficiency. Thereby, GMPPT depends on the design of the PV system. Quadruple MPPT exhibited more efficient results compared to the other MPPT models in addition to many merits. This paper focuses on making the photovoltaic system operate at maximum possible power under partial shading conditions by using quadruple MPP trackers to achieve the convergence towards the GMPP.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of DS/SS-CDMA Transmission Technique for Connected Objects in IoT Domain
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper we present a design an analysis of DS/SS-CDMA (Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum Code Division Multiple Access) transceiver system for Connected Objects using MATLAB/Simulink. DS/SS-CDMA transmission system is one of the systems to perform the above requirement in IoT (Internet of Things). To design the DS/SS-CDMA transceiver, different codes in different modulation techniques were used. We have designed a MISO (Multiple Input Single Output) DS/SS-CDMA transmitter and receiver for BPSK (Binary Phase Shift Keying), QPSK (Quadrature Phase Shift Keying), modulation schemes, using M and Gold Sequence Codes. The system performance was evaluated by calculation of Bit Error Rate (BER), comparing the received and transmitted data.

articleTitle: Electrical and Molecular Engineering of π-Conjugated Polymers for Multilayer OLED Application
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, a combined theoretical and experimental study into the properties of two π -conjugated polymers with different spacers were investigated. Theoretical calculations were performed using density functional theory (DFT), TDDFT and Marcus theories, to predict the optoelectronic and charge transport properties. As a result, polymer with thiophene spacer shows good optical properties and green emission with a maximum wavelength λemis=508 nm. These results are in good agreement with the experimental data. Furthermore, the calculated results show that thiophene polymer has better electron and hole mobility equal to 7.32 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 3.10 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, respectively. Using these properties, current-voltage characteristics of a multilayer organic light emitting diode based on the studied polymers are performed using a physically based device simulator Silvaco Atlas. Good electrical properties are obtained for thiophene polymer compared to phenylene with a turn-on voltage equal to 5.9 V.

articleTitle: Remote Control Package for Kuka Robots using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Kuka is one of the leading innovative companies in the manufacturing of industrial robots. However, they lack of direct communication with PC in order to send and receive data. To overcome this drawback, Kuka offers additional communication packages to establish the needed communication. However, this communication package requires calculating the forward and inverse kinematics or additional hardware (PLCs). Then sending the data as an XML file to the Kuka controller. This paper is dedicated to use KukaVarproxy package to establish connection between a Kuka robot and MATLAB. Thus, users can program the robot through MATLAB without using any additional software provided by Kuka (RSI, mxA). The paper focuses on developing a MATLAB package, which users can use to program the robot without requiring to use KRL. Also, the implemented functions allow the user to program the robot without the need of any mathematical information about the robot.

articleTitle: Relaxed Stabilization Conditions for Time Delayed Takagi-Sugeno Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper tackles the stabilization of Takagi Sugeno (TS) fuzzy systems with time delay. In this work, we will use a weighted function to bound the time-derivative of membership functions. In addition, we will introduce slack matrices to obtain more flexible stability conditions from a computational point of view. Then, the stability approach will be extended to design a control that ensure the global closed loop stability for the time-delayed T-S system. Finally, real application (truck-trailer) is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: On the Parallel Processing for Wireless Sensors Converged Network
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper studies the capability of multi-parallel processing to be accommodated in machine-to-machine communications. A testbed convergence between the wireless sensor network and the wireless mobile network is performed. It deals with enhancing wireless mobile network performance. This testbed is divided into three stages; combating the peak-to-average power ratio problem, observing a real data making use of an actual wireless sensors, and proposing a multi-parallel processing communications. The mentioned testbed above is done in a realistic academic environment, where selected signals from those sensors are evaluated. Thus, a design improvement is detailed in terms of the peak-to-average power ratio and the efficient use of the limited resources. In particular, the scope focuses on the mitigation of the nonlinear distortion and its effect on bit error rate. The validation process is attained based on performing an extensive simulation. It is observing some certain performance parameters such as the sensor life time, and the consumed energy. From the testbed simulation results, the proposed work shows promising results comparing to the conventional wireless sensor network. The delay reduction reaches around 85%, while the peak to average power ratio values has improved by 42.3%.

articleTitle: Control of a grid connected photovoltaic systems using classical controller
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper propose a schema of a grid connected PV control in order to provide a maximum power and high quality of current injected into the grid. Our article deals with the modeling and control of a photovoltaic chain connected to the grid. In This paper, we present the model of all the elements of the photovoltaic chain as well as the control of the different converters. The controllers used to control the inverter are conventional PI controllers. An LCL filter is used connect the inverter to the grid.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Based Task Scheduling of Mobile Robots in Flexible Manufacturing Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The main objective of this research work is to design and evaluate real time intelligent scheduling algorithms for flexible manufacturing systems. The proposed system has set of programmable CNC machines, load and unload stations, group of mobile robots for material handling, and robot charging station. Each machine, station and robot is considered as a node in a wireless sensor network. Information between FMS units are transferred through a wireless sensor network and used by the main controller. Intelligent algorithms are required to manage and control the FMS environment for tasks scheduling and robot routing. Several simulated case studies will be considered to test and verify the flexibility of the system and the capability of the proposed algorithms to use effectively available machines and mobile robots. Encouraging results are achieved when the performance of the proposed scheduling algorithms is compared with others obtained from similar systems in published literature.

articleTitle: Application of learning algorithm for Diabetic Retinopathy Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: One of the causes of blindness among working-age adults is the diabetic retinopathy (DR). The DR raise the damage of the retina if it is not early diagnosed and treated. In the present paper, we are focusing on the detection of the primary signs of the diabetic retinopathy which is the exudate. The exudate appeared in white or yellow color with different shapes, sizes and positions. More its position is close to the optic disk, more the percentage of blindness is increased. That's why the position and the size are two important information for an ophthalmologist to distinguish or diagnose the severity of the disease. For those reasons, we aim in this paper to detect and segment the exudate using Random Forest classifier. A DR database used with the application of a Random Forest classifier to segment these regions. The impact of varying the main parameter of the random forest algorithm is studied. We achieved the highest value of the specificity and the accuracy with 99.5% and 99.50% respectively. An area under curve (AUC) of 0.952 is obtained.

articleTitle: Iron Loss Mionimization of a PMSM Using Flux Barriers
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Recently, permanent magnet motors have been progressively considered the most practical in many applications in order to diminish the pollution level and to solve oil costs problem. Thus, pertinent researches have been performed to ameliorate their performances. The present work deals with the improvement of the main performances of a fractional slot concentrated windings permanent magnet motor. To achieve this goal, magnetic flux barriers method has been applied in the stator yoke in order to decrease and possibly to eliminate low space harmonics of the air gap flux density. The proposed solution has been contributed to the reduction of rotor losses caused by the armature reaction field. Simulation results show considerable advantages over the conventional motor.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Parameter Estimation for Wiener-Hammerstein Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method to estimate the unknown parameters for stochastic nonlinear systems that can be described by Wiener-Hammerstein (W-H) mathematical models (L-N-L cascade). The key of this technique is to decompose the W-H structure into three sub-blocks. Afterwards, we apply the Recursive Extended Least Squares (RELS) estimator at each discrete-time in order to estimate the unknown parameters. Next, we put the output system under two matrix forms and from that, we determine the others parameters using the predicted intermediate variables. The convergence analysis of the W-H-RHPE algorithm is made using the differential equation approach and its performance is validated by treating a simulation example.

articleTitle: Control Structure for a Photovoltaic Chain Connected to the Three-phase Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper aims to model a photovoltaic panel and control it when connecting to the three-phase grid. The system contains a photovoltaic panel and a boost converter (DC/DC) controlled by maximum power point tracking (MPPT) used perturbation and observation algorithm (P & O). Its purpose is to extract the maximum power from the solar panel. The assembly is connected to the grid via a voltage inverter and a low-pass filter (L r) in order to inject the active power of the photovoltaic into the three phase grid. The regulation of the voltage Vdc, the direct and quadratic component of the currents is carried out by a classic regulator (PI). The model is simulated using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Signed Regressor LMMN Algorithm for complex-valued data
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This work reports expressions for different parameters constituting the main support for convergence of the signed regressor least mean mixed-norm (LMMN) algorithm for complex-valued data. The steady-state mean-square error, the optimum step-size, and the corresponding minimum value of the tracking mean-square error are all derived. Simulation results are conducted to corroborate the theoretical findings. Also, the convergence behaviour of the signed regressor LMMN algorithm and that of the LMMN algorithm are compared.

articleTitle: A computational study to the optoelectronic properties of Al Schiff base complex for Efficient OLED
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this work, a Schiff base complex derived from ninhydrin-glycine ligand (NG) with Al (III) metal was designed. Detailed optoelectronic investigations are performed using experimental measurement and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Good agreement between the calculated results and the experimental ones is achieved. Furthermore, Marcus theories is used to predict the charge transport properties in order to estimate the possibility of introducing this compound in OLED devices. The calculated results showed that AI-NG has good and balance electron and hole charge transfer with an intermolecular charge hopping rates equal to 4.10 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> and 4.86 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>, respectively. Using these interesting calculated properties an ITO/ AI-NG/AI: LiF OLED device is numerically simulated using Silvaco Atlas 2-D software. The device shows a good electrical behavior with a turn-on voltage equal to 6.9 V.

articleTitle: Fault detection of uncertain nonlinear process using interval-valued data-driven approach
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Kernel PCA (KPCA) has been extensively applied in fault detection (FD) field. However, it is constantly not optimal for uncertain systems and is not designed to handle large-scale process monitoring. Thus, a nonlinear fault detection (FD) method based interval reduced KPCA (IRKPCA) is developed for fault detection. The proposed IRKPCA technique uses interval-valued Euclidean distance as a criterion to maintain only the more pertinent measurements. The FD abilities of the IRKPCA technique is assessed using the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP). The effectiveness of the proposed technique is assessed in terms of computation time (CT), false alarm rate (FAR)and missed detection rate (MDR).

articleTitle: Multi-criteria decision making for reconductoring overhead lines
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The multi-criteria decision method AHP (Analytical Hierarchy Process) is adopted to propose the best HTLS overhead conductor for reconductoring the 225 kV lines used in the Tunisian network and to give a greater electric-current-carrying capability to meet the power demand. Including a set of technical, economic and environmental considerations, the AHP is applied to compare seven HTLS conductors' technologies with different weighting scenarios for studying the sensitivity of the classifying results and to find the best compromise.

articleTitle: Investigation the Performance Effect of Adjacent and Co-Channel Interferences on AWGN and Rayleigh Channels Using16-QAM Modulation
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Interference is a phenomena communication systems have to live with. It cannot be completely eliminated but measures have to be taken to minimize their effect. Sources of interference are additional mobile in the identical cell, a call in progress in neighboring cell, and other base station (BS) working in the similar frequency band. Interference is a limiting factor in all communication systems since it increases the dropped calls rate in the cellular radio systems which in turn limits these system's capacity and this of course degrades the communication system quality. There a care full attention must be taken to mitigate the effect of interference when considering designing and implementing communication systems. Interference can take one of two forms Adjacent Channel Interference (ACI) or Co-Channel Interference (CCI) or both. To investigate and analyze the performance effect of these two interferences on AWGN and Rayleigh communication channels for data communication. The 16 - Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (16-QAM) technique is considered in this paper since this scheme of modulation is one of the M-ary QAM modulation which has a good performance in wireless frequency bands, and widely used in wireless communication systems. In this work the effect of these interferences is investigated, and simulated on AWGN and Rayleigh. using Simulink.

articleTitle: EE-SE Trade-off Optimization for Downlink NOMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: As a potential multiple access scheme for future radio access, Non Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) has been considered as an emerging radio access technique for the fifth-generation (5G) wireless communications. Green Radio (GR), which focuses on Energy Efficiency (EE), is becoming an inevitable trend for future wireless network design. Recent works have concentrated on the relationship between EE and SE and provided good thoughts into the EE-SE trade-off. In this paper, we study the EE-SE trade-off problem for NOMA systems in downlink. The trade-off problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization topic in which the main idea is to maximize the EE by imposing a satisfying minimum SE The Quality of Service (QoS) requirement for each user is also introduced to ensure optimality. For this, an optimal power allocation is proposed. Through simulations, we demonstrate the proposed schemes efficiency in achieving a flexible trade-off between EE and SE.

articleTitle: Incipient Broken Bar Detection Using Information Entropy of Second Generation Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In the last decades, the improvement of availability of industrial processes has become crucial. Hence, the diagnosis and the fault detection of the machinery has become considered essential in order to guarantee high performances of the plant operation. Since induction machines dominate all drives, their health management (HM) has received high attentions. Despite the persistent usage of double cage induction machines (DCIM), their HM suffers from a lack of research focus. The advances in signal processing tools inspire this work at the aim of diagnosing one of the most hardly detected defects of DCIM. In fact, the challenge in the diagnosis of the DCIM is the early detection of the breakage of the outer cage's bar. This work represents a new alternative using the Information Entropy of the Second Generation Wavelet Transform (SGWT). Based on the Current Analysis, numerous severity levels of broken rotor bar are analyzed including the incipient broken outer cage's bar under several load levels. The concluded results validate the competency of this approach.

articleTitle: Application of Autonomous Group Particle Swarm Optimization for Optimal PMUs Placement
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The optimal location of phase measurement units (PMUs) indicates the strategic placement of PM Us to obtain full observability of the power systems with a reduced number of PMUs. It is necessary to have a strategic placement due to the economic or technical limitations that hinder the placement of PMU s in each bus. A modified version of particle swarm optimization called Autonomous Particles Groups for Particle Swarm optimization (AGPSO) is proposed in this paper, for placing the PMUs that ensure full power system observability in the presence of zero injection bus and single PMU loss, while maximizing the measurement redundancy. The proposed AGPSO has been applied to the IEEE 14, 24 and NE 39-bus. The outcomes show that the number of PMU s is similar to or less than the corresponding results of recently published papers, while the system topological observability is complete.

articleTitle: VFD fed Induction Motor Fault Detection using Drive's data and Harmonic Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Although the successful use of various variants of the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) in the field of fault detection in Direct On-Line (DOL) fed Induction Motors, new challenges rise with the widespread use of Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) in industrial application. Regardless of the fault detection technique, the permanent variation in the fundamental frequency and therefore the fault frequencies of the analyzed signal imply a permanent re-tuning of DWT in terms of coefficient bandwidth and mother wavelet parameter. This tuning is a trial-and-error process which rises practical problem in the context of on-line Condition Monitoring Systems (CMS). Considering these limitations, the DWT use is non-tailored to the context of a VFD fed IM on-line CMS. In this paper, a novel auto-tunable DWT called the Windowed Harmonic Wavelet Packet Transform (WHWPT) using drive's data is presented in order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks. The new approach has been validated experimentally using broken rotor bar fault in a VFD fed 3-kW Double Cage IM under a power supply at different fundamental frequencies. Fault feature extraction results show the robustness and the flexibility of the proposed approach through clear distinction between healthy and faulty motor conditions even for several fundamental frequencies.

articleTitle: Dynamic “Energy sharing model” in multi-source and multi-consumer collaborative Smart micro-Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Despite the importance of the renewable energies and its positive impacts on the environmental and economic fields, its installation still very expensive for many type of consumers. The collaborative funding, to install renewable energies resources, can be an interest solution, especially, for the consumers how share a common space like common building roofs, common gardens, common site … etc. However, collaborative energy cannot succeed without a good management system which will be more complicated if it manages multi-source and multi-consumers with different collaboration rates. In this paper, we propose a new mathematical “energy sharing model” adapted for collaborative renewable energies installation, which can computes the renewable energy part of each user dynamically and redistributes the unused energy proportionally. The proposed solution can reduce effectively the energy storage and gives an important benefit of renewable energies for every user. The simulation results show that for a 7.5% average of collaboration, the user can get 11% as profit, in an explanation case, which means his allowed renewable energy reach 18.5%. And in the better case, he can reach 92.45% of benefit.

articleTitle: Observability Bound of Discrete Linear Singularly Perturbed System
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper treats the observability bound problem of discrete linear singularly perturbed system (SPS). Using appropriate Lyapunov functionals, satisfactory conditions formulated in term of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs) are elaborated to analyse the asymptotic stability of the system in one hand and in the other hand to prove the asymptotic stability of the observation error system. A luenberger observer is used to achieve this task. Illustrative numerical example is provided to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: Discrete time linear Singularly Perturbed System

articleTitle: No-ReferenceColor Image Quality Assessment Using HOSVD Based Features and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Images and videos are seen as the most reliable source of visual information as they are a fundamental part of the multimedia world. For instance, face recognition technology utilizes images for security purposes. However, due to either the physical properties of the acquisition equipment (internal) or the nature of the environment (external), images can be affected by a wide range of distortions. Researchers have enumerated more than 24 distortions that can affect images. Among which four types are the most prominent ones. In this paper, a novel no-reference color image quality assessment technique is introduced. The technique is based on extracting a set of features from the High Order Singular Value Decomposition (HOSVD) of images. Such features are then used with a neural network regressor to predict the quality score. The results show excellent performance exceeding traditional techniques based only on gray-scale images.

articleTitle: Causal ordering Graph based observers for generating redundant relations
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper deals with a new causal graph-based fault detection scheme. The Causal Ordering Graph (COG) is herein involved to rise above difficulties of modeling dynamic systems due to both qualitative and quantitative reasonings. For the fault detection purpose, the generic model in natural (or integral) causality is apt to design the COG observers in Luenberger forms. Compared with classical observers-based fault detection, the developed scheme allows to get graphical representation taking in to account the physical aspects (the transit of information and the energy transfer) related to the system mechanism. Owing to energetic and structural aspects, the COG observer gain is determined via causal manipulations (causal loops, causal paths ... etc). The relevance of the suggested framework is proved through the simulation results on the hydraulic system with two tanks.

articleTitle: Possibilistic Feature Selection Method based on Discriminant Power for Class Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Feature selection is important for the reduction of computing complexity especially in systems dealing with a high amount of data. In this context, various interesting methods of feature selection based on possibilistic model have been proposed. Some of them suffer from system divergence in case of high number of features. In this paper, we propose a feature selection method for class discrimination based on a possibilistic data modeling. In fact, possibilistic modeling is a powerful paradigm, which is able to handle data imperfection. The proposed approach is based on two discriminant levels in order to extract features that are able to discriminate between two classes. The first level depends on the discriminant power of two possibilistic distributions. This level is enhanced by a cross-validation concept. The second level depends on the scoring rate relative of each feature. The approach is validated using synthetic data sets and benchmark data sets. The obtained results show the ability of the proposed approach in selecting the most significant features.

articleTitle: Original Structural and Electrical Investigation for a New $\mathbf{BG-F}_{6}$ Vitreous Bio-Ceramic as Humidity Sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Two biomaterial types have been the focus of sensor applications: Fluorosilicate bioactive Glass BG-F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> crude and compact. Of the two, BG-F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> compact material show the greater mechanical strength, and electrical behaviour provoke greater humidity sensing capacity. Thus, the glassy discs show great potential for deployment in a new generation of biosensors and environment requires. The aim of this paper is to develop a material that combines an interesting mechanical strength, monophasic stability with potential thermic resistance and great electrical capacity. By returning to its high temperature synthesis protocol, makes this fluorosilicate glass an attractive material for sensors development topic and environmental precautions.

articleTitle: Research on feature extraction method based on brain network and CSP for MI-EEG signals
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: At present, most of the classification studies on EEG signals of motor imagination focus on the classification of left and right hands. In this paper, a feature analysis method based on the combination of brain functional network and common spatial pattern is proposed to solve the dichotomy of unilateral (right) hand motor imagination. Firstly, the phase analysis between Mu rhythm and Beta rhythm signals is carried out, and then the brain functional network topology is drawn according to the phase synchronization information matrix. Through analysis, Mu rhythm of MI - EEG signals than Beta rhythm is more active, and phase synchronization oscillation is concentrated in the center of the brain area C, FC and CP. Then, the concept of graph theory is used to extract the network attribute features under two rhythms: clustering coefficient and shortest path length, and the common space mode method is used to extract the spatial domain features, and the two types of features form an 8-dimensional feature vector. Finally, the features are classified by SVM, and the average classification accuracy is 94.69%, which is higher than that of the two methods. The research content of this paper breaks through the traditional right-handed MI-EEG classification problem, and the method in this paper does not need to consider the ERD/ERS phenomenon, thus expanding the range of data that can be classified.

articleTitle: Study of bistability behavior relative to the size of the composite plates
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Nowadays, the improvement of the nonlinearity for energy harvesting systems is more and more investigated due to their ability to work for a wider frequency range. For this purpose, in this work, the development of bistable plates is proposed. In particular, the properties of composite bistable boards, built of monolayers of ordered carbon fibers is investigated. This paper proposes a bistable plates, where this effect is introduced during the manufacturing by changing the orientation of individual layers. In particular, the effect of the plate size and thickness on the bistability is studied experimentally. For this purpose, the relationship of the force F relative to x, where x is a measure of the plate deflection relative to the unstable equilibrium point (at plate). Further, the potential energy Ep(x) is evaluated through the numerical integration of the force characteristic to deduce the effect of the studied parameters on the plates bistability.

articleTitle: Potential of carbonaceous materials for the realization of high performance sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 17th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
